 Dated this the 10th day of December, 2024
 Judgment

The legal heirs of deceased Nafeesu, who died in a road accident on 24.11.2016, have come up in the present appeal dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation granted by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tirur.

2. On 24.11.2016 at 9.30 p.m., when the deceased was walking through the left side of Kuttippuram - Chamravattom Bypass road, a goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KL-65-F-3134 driven in a rash and negligent manner from Ponnani - Pallapram side, hit against the deceased and knocked her down.
As a result of the accident, the deceased sustained fatal injuries and was admitted to the Jubilee Hospital, Thrissur.
From there she was referred to Aswini Hospital, Thrissur.
While undergoing treatment there, she succumbed to the injuries on 27.11.2016.

sentences.text: The claimants contended that she was working as an Agriculturalist, also having a milk business and was earning a 2024:KER:93702 monthly income of Rs.12,000/-.

The Tribunal, however, fixed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,500/- and granted the following compensation:

4. Heard, Sri.T.C.Suresh Menon - learned counsel appearing for the appellants and Sri.P.K.Manoj Kumar - learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company.
5. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal could not have taken the notional income at Rs.8,500/-.

He relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme 2024:KER:93702 Court in Civil Appeal No.10950/2024 [Angad Tiwari and Another v. National Insurance Company Ltd. and Another] decided on 01.10.2024 to contend that at any rate, the income of the deceased cannot be fixed below the minimum wage.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

He further submitted that in Rakesh Swarup Saxena v.
New India Assurance Company Ltd. [2023 ACJ 2680], the Hon'ble Apex Court held that in respect of death of a lady of the house, to the family a global compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- has to be granted in addition to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at the High Court.
6.

entities.text:
Rakesh Swarup Saxena v.
New India Assurance Company Ltd. [2023 ACJ 2680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company pointed out that the award rendered by the Tribunal is just and proper, and does not call for any interference by this Court.
He further pointed out that, even going by the averments in the claim petition, the claim of the claimants is only for fixation of the income at Rs.12,000/-.
Therefore, even if this Court is inclined to fix the notional income suitably, it cannot go beyond Rs.12,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the rival submissions raised across the Bar and have perused the award impugned in the appeal.

In G.O.(P)No.56/2017/Fin. dated 28.04.2017, the State of Kerala has prescribed the minimum wages liable to be paid under the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, with the effect from 01.04.2017.
The minimum wage, in accordance with the Government Order, is Rs.17,325/-.

Therefore, if this Court is to apply the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Angad Tiwari (supra), the minimum wage in respect of deceased Nafeesu has to be fixed at Rs.17,325/-.
9.
However, having said so, this Court will have to consider the contentions raised on behalf of the learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company.
It is true that in the petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, only an amount of Rs.12,000/- has been claimed.
However, this need not deter this Court from proceeding to fix the notional income suitably.

In Bimla Devi and Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others [(2009) 13 SCC 530], the Hon'ble Apex Court held that strict proof of pleadings cannot be insisted in an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text:
Bimla Devi and Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others [(2009) 13 SCC 530]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the categoric pronouncements of law by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this Court has no hesitation to hold that 2024:KER:93702 the pleadings in a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is irrelevant while fixing the notional income of the claimants or the deceased in accordance with the provisions.
At any rate, this Court is certainly bound by the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Angad Tiwari (supra).

Therefore, this Court has no hesitation to reject the contention on behalf of the Insurance Company and proceeds to holds that the income of the deceased Nafeesu has to be fixed at Rs.17,325/-.
10.
As regards the claim for fixation of global enhancement of Rs.2,50,000/-, it is pertinent to note that the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2 lakhs towards loss of love and affection to all the claimants.

Going by the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Company Ltd. v. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur [(2021) 11 SCC 780], once the compensation towards loss of consortium is granted, a separate compensation towards loss of love and affection cannot be granted.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd. v. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur [(2021) 11 SCC 780]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, if the principles laid down in Rakesh Swarup Saxena (supra) is applied,
then certainly, the compensation granted under the head loss of love and 2024:KER:93702 affection could be shifted to the compensation towards global enhancement.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the claimants/appellants are entitled for further enhancement of Rs.50,000/-.
11. In respect of the claim for consortium is concerned, a perusal of the award of the Tribunal shows that there were four claimants.

The 2nd claimant, who is the son of deceased and 3 rd claimant,
being the daughter of the deceased, had not been granted any compensation towards filial consortium.

The cause of action adopted by the Tribunal cannot be accepted in the light of the judgment rendered by this Court in United India Insurance Company v. Shalumol [2021 (5) KHC 28], i.e. a married daughter is certainly entitled for the benefit of loss of consortium.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company v. Shalumol [2021 (5) KHC 28]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, going by the dictum laid down by Tribunal by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Birender and Others [(2020) 11 SCC 356], the married sons are also entitled for the benefit under the head loss of consortium.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are awarded an additional compensation of Rs.15,58,752/- (Rupees fifteen lakhs fifty eight thousand seven hundred fifty two only) over and above the compensation awarded by the Tribunal with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till realization together with proportionate costs.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

While, calculating 2024:KER:93702 interest, it is ordered that the appellants will not be entitled for interest for a period of 180 days,
which represents the period of delay in filing the appeal.
The appeal is allowed accordingly.
